# Recon Craft — layout-tests-reuse

*Source of record — do not edit. Distilled into the spec by `/spec create`.*

Greenfield: there is no house style to match, so the family this code joins is Cloudflare's
current templates and docs, grammY's guidance, and the best-kept open-source grammY bots.
Three web-research agents, 2026-11-16, worked against the locked stack (waves 1–2): TypeScript,
grammY, Cloudflare Workers Free, one SQLite Durable Object per chat. [unverified] = community
source only; [inferred] = read from source, not run. Exemplar codes are listed at the end.

## Layout and naming

### Settled by Cloudflare's templates and docs
- `wrangler.jsonc` (Cloudflare "recommends using `wrangler.jsonc` for new projects"; CF-CONFIG,
  C3) with `$schema`, `exports` + `durable_objects.bindings`, and `secrets.required`, which lets
  `wrangler types` type the secrets without `.dev.vars`, so CI can generate types.
- `worker-configuration.d.ts` at the root, generated by `wrangler types` and committed; it declares
  `Cloudflare.Env` (C3 `src/workers.ts`, CF-TS). `wrangler types --check` exits 1 when it is
  stale ("Useful for CI/CD").
- Base on C3-HW for `tsconfig.json` (`moduleResolution: "Bundler"`, `es2024`,
  `include: ["worker-configuration.d.ts","src/**/*.ts"]`), `test/` with `test/tsconfig.json`,
  `vitest.config.mts`, and scripts `dev` / `deploy` / `test` / `cf-typegen`. C3-DO is stale
  (wrangler ^3, `moduleResolution: "node"`, no tests): take only its class shape.
- `.dev.vars` for local secrets, `.dev.vars.example` committed, `.gitignore` as in C3-DO
  (`.dev.vars*`, `!.dev.vars.example`, `.wrangler/`). Use `.dev.vars` or `.env`, not both (CF-SECRETS).
- Durable Object schema (RULES): migrations run in the constructor inside `blockConcurrencyWhile`,
  tracked in `_sql_schema_migrations(id, applied_at)`; "`PRAGMA user_version` is not supported".
  Tables snake_case plural, `*_at` columns, `idx_<table>_<col>`.
- Under `exports`, a class "is ignored until you declare it in `exports`" and must be exported from
  the main module, hence a re-export from `src/index.ts` (CF-MIG).
- Workers Builds settings live in the dashboard, not the repo, and non-production branches default
  to `npx wrangler preview`; checks need their own `.github/workflows/` file (CF-BUILDS).

### grammY and the bots
- grammY prescribes one `Composer` per feature module, assembled in `bot.ts` (GY-S).
- Files are kebab-case `.ts` (BB, WS, OC, NK, CFA, CFV); exports are named, with `export default`
  only for the Worker handler object (C3-DO, GY-S, BB, WS, RR, NK).
- Factories `createBot()`, `createXKeyboard()`; constants SCREAMING_SNAKE (`ALLOWED_UPDATES`,
  `WEBHOOK_PATH`); env `BOT_TOKEN`, `BOT_INFO` (grammY Workers guide).
- Durable Object class: PascalCase noun, binding SCREAMING_SNAKE (`ChatRoom` / `CHAT_ROOM` in
  RULES). `Chat` collides with grammY's `Chat` type (`@grammyjs/types` manage.ts).
- No popular bot runs grammY in a per-chat object; the Workers exemplars have ≤21★ (RR, NK, NY).

### Unit → path (feature-first; layer-first is decision C1)
| Unit | Proposed path | Follows |
|---|---|---|
| Worker entry | `src/index.ts`: `export default { fetch } satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>`, re-exports the object class | C3-DO `src/index.ts`; CFA `src/index.ts` |
| Chat Durable Object | `src/chat/chat-room.ts`, `ChatRoom extends DurableObject<Env>`, binding `CHAT_ROOM` | RULES; NK `src/storage/*.do.ts` |
| Migrations | `src/chat/schema.ts`, an ordered `{ id, description, sql }[]` | RULES; DU README; ACT `packages/storage/src/sql-schema-migrations.ts` |
| Timed jobs | `src/chat/jobs.ts` | NY `src/lib/schedule.ts`; Agents verbs `schedule` / `cancelSchedule` |
| Bot assembly | `src/bot.ts`: `createBot()`, one `bot.use()` per feature | GY-S; RR `src/bot.ts`; NK `src/bot/create-bot.ts` |
| Context type | `src/context.ts` | BB, NK `src/bot/context.ts` |
| Roster, join/leave | `src/members/member-handlers.ts`, `member-store.ts` | NK `<feature>-handlers.ts`; WS `src/handlers/user-and-chat-sync-handler.ts` |
| /all | `src/members/all-handlers.ts` | WS `src/commands/<cmd>.ts` |
| /domikpisik | `src/stats/domikpisik-handlers.ts` | same |
| /pool, /join, /pools | `src/pools/pool-handlers.ts` | NK `src/profile/profile-handlers.ts` |
| ✅ ❌ 🔔 🎲 buttons | `src/pools/pool-callbacks.ts` | NK `src/suggestions/suggestion-callbacks.ts`; OC `*-callback-handler.ts` |
| Pool rules (pure) | `src/pools/pool-rules.ts` | GY-S `src/todo/item.ts`; RR `rollReply()` returns a value, `bot.ts` does the I/O |
| Pool SQL | `src/pools/pool-store.ts` | NK `*-service.ts`; NY `src/lib/repository.ts` |
| /pool arguments, Kyiv start time | `src/pools/pool-args.ts` | WS `src/util/parse-leaderboard-input.ts`; RR `src/notation.ts` |
| Pool card, keyboard | `src/pools/pool-format.ts`, `pool-keyboards.ts` | NK `src/stats/stats-format.ts`, `src/profile/profile-keyboards.ts` |
| /stats | `src/stats/stats-handlers.ts` | WS `src/commands/stats.ts` |
| Stats queries, leaderboards | `src/stats/stats-queries.ts`, `stats-format.ts` | NK `src/stats/stats-reader.ts`, `stats-format.ts` |
| Mentions | `src/members/mentions.ts` | OC `src/bot/messages/telegram-text.ts`; WS `src/util/escape-html-entities.ts` |
| Ukrainian strings | `src/texts.ts`, one typed object | RR `src/locales/uk.ts`; NK `src/i18n/messages.ts` |
| `ALLOWED_UPDATES`, `COMMANDS` | `src/telegram.ts`, shared with the setup script | RR `src/telegram.ts`; OC `src/bot/commands/definitions.ts` |
| setWebhook, setMyCommands | `scripts/configure-telegram.ts`, npm script `telegram:configure` | RR `scripts/configure-telegram.ts`; NY `scripts/telegram-*.ts` |
| CI checks | `.github/workflows/check.yml` | NK, NY |

Gotchas: object migrations don't belong in a root `migrations/` folder, which is D1's default
`migrations_dir` [inferred]. Node runs a `.ts` script only with explicit file extensions in imports
and without enums, namespaces or parameter properties (nodejs.org/api/typescript.html), so a script
importing `src/telegram.ts` constrains src's import style. The C3 scaffold isn't Prettier-clean
(double quotes against its own `singleQuote: true`).

## Tests and fixtures

### Runner
- `@cloudflare/vitest-plugin` 1.8.3 replaced `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` (last 0.23.0) on
  2026-08-20; it needs `vitest ^4.1.0 || ^5.0.0` (latest 5.1.0). Config:
  `defineConfig({ plugins: [cloudflareTest({ wrangler: { configPath: "./wrangler.jsonc" } })] })`.
  `defineWorkersConfig`, `poolOptions.workers`, `isolatedStorage` and `singleWorker` are gone
  (developers.cloudflare.com/workers/testing/vitest-integration/migration-guides/). Most online
  guides predate this.
- "Storage isolation is per test file"; files run concurrently, and tests in one file share
  Durable Object state (…/vitest-integration/isolation-and-concurrency/).
- APIs: `env` and `exports` from `cloudflare:workers` (`exports.default.fetch` replaces the deprecated
  `SELF.fetch`); from `cloudflare:test`: `runInDurableObject`, `runDurableObjectAlarm` (returns
  `false` when no alarm is set), `evictDurableObject`, `listDurableObjectIds`, `reset()`,
  `createExecutionContext`, `waitOnExecutionContext` (…/test-apis/). The C3 starter still imports
  the deprecated `env` / `SELF`.
- Outbound mocking: `fetchMock` is removed; `@msw/cloudflare` 0.2.0 + `msw` 3.0.6 patch the global
  `fetch` (…/mock-outbound-requests/; fixture `request-mocking/test/`). grammY captures `fetch` in
  its ApiClient constructor, so a Bot built before `network.enable()` bypasses MSW [inferred].
- Exemplar tests: workers-sdk `fixtures/vitest-plugin-examples/durable-objects/test/alarm.test.ts`
  (seed state with `runInDurableObject`, fire with `runDurableObjectAlarm`), `sqlite-in-do.test.ts`,
  and `durable-objects-exports/`.
- Known issues: dynamic `import()` fails inside object handlers; every response body must be read;
  the coverage docs say Istanbul while the changelog fixed V8 (…/known-issues/).

### Faking Telegram
- grammY's own suite stubs `bot.api.getMe` and `globalThis.fetch`, types fixtures as
  `botInfo: UserFromGetMe` and `testUpdate: Update`, and builds commands with
  `entities: [{ type: "bot_command", offset: 0, length: 6 }]` (grammY `test/bot.test.ts`,
  `test/composer.test.ts`).
- A transformer may answer `{ ok: true, … }` without calling `prev` (grammy.dev/advanced/transformers).
  Workers exemplar github.com/ArnaudRinquin/daily-games (1★, grammY 1.46, a bot for a group of
  friends): `test/worker/handlers.test.ts` has `testBot()` with
  `bot.api.config.use(async (_prev, method, payload) => { calls.push(…); return { ok: true, result } })`,
  update builders `dm()`, `command()`, `groupMessage()`, a `seq` id counter and a fixed `AT`; its
  `vitest.config.ts` binds a fake `BOT_TOKEN`, so an unstubbed call fails instead of messaging people.
- Helper libraries `grammy-testing` 0.26.0 (one release, 7★), `@bonkers-agency/grammy-test` 0.1.3 and
  `telegram-test-api` 4.2.1 (2022): none shown working on workerd.
- Types: `@grammyjs/types` 5.0.0, pinned and re-exported by grammy 1.46.0 as `grammy/types`.

### Time and randomness
- `Date.now()` "returns the time of the last I/O" and "does not advance during code execution"
  (developers.cloudflare.com/workers/reference/security-model/).
- `vi.useFakeTimers` / `vi.setSystemTime` work in the runner but never move Durable Object alarms
  (workers-sdk#5394, closed as not planned on 2026-11-13).
- cloudflare/agents' tests: pure timing functions take `now` (`src/tests/schedules/timing.test.ts`);
  object tests backdate stored rows, re-arm, then call `runDurableObjectAlarm`; each test uses its
  own object name.
- Nothing seeds randomness; `crypto.getRandomValues` is available; workerd refuses random values at
  global scope [unverified]. No exemplar injects a draw.

### CI
- With `test/` excluded from the root tsconfig, typecheck twice: `tsc --noEmit` and
  `tsc --noEmit -p test`; add `wrangler types --check`.
- Node: Vitest 5.1 needs `^22.12 || ^24 || >=26`; Workers Builds defaults to Node 24.22.1 and reads
  `.nvmrc` (…/workers/ci-cd/builds/build-image/), so one `.nvmrc` serves Builds and `setup-node`.
- TypeScript 7.0.2 (the native compiler, 2026-07-08) is npm's `latest`; C3 pins `^5.5.2`;
  typescript-eslint does not support 7 yet [unverified].
- Workers Builds posts GitHub check runs; whether it waits for Actions, or a failing build command
  blocks the deploy, is undocumented. Alternative: `cloudflare/wrangler-action@v4` deploying after
  the tests pass (daily-games).

## Extraction, reuse, don't-build

### Pure modules from day one (no grammY or storage imports; `now` and the RNG passed in)
| # | Module | Holds | Test cost | Prior art |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | Pool rules | answers → players (first N by join time), bench in order, passed, unanswered (roster minus answered); a drop-out promotes the bench head and returns who to ping; the one-time draw (RNG in, used flag); "just became full"; close time (start or open + 3 h); the /join target (newest open pool) | medium | PartitelleBot `domain/participation.py`: `decide_join` / `decide_leave` return a `Change` with `reached_target`, applied by the caller |
| E2 | Roster rules | who counts as a member (writers, plus `chat_member` joins, minus leaves, no bots); /all = roster minus the caller | low | chat-members docs: the API can't list members, so "keep track of them yourself" |
| E3 | Stats windows, leaderboards | a Kyiv calendar month → `[startMs, endMs)`; ranking and ties for the five boards; total joins | low | PartitelleBot `migrations/0005_participation_event.sql`; PUBobot2 `/top` |
| E4 | /pool parser, start time | tokens → {game, size, start or now}; Kyiv wall time → instant; a time already past; the DST gap and overlap | low, table-driven | PartitelleBot `domain/schedule.py` |
| E5 | Mentions | [{id, name}] → mention pieces in chunks (≤5 until the live test), caller excluded | low (names with `<`, `&`, emoji) | AnjanaMadu: batches of 5, 2 s apart |
| E6 | Card, keyboard, callback codec | pool view → text or entities + inline keyboard, `action:poolId` ≤64 bytes; deterministic, so an unchanged edit can be skipped and a stale one re-rendered | low, golden outputs | PartitelleBot `behaviours/edit_summary.py`; PadelDubaiBot `message-formatter.ts` |
| E7 | Job planner (if scheduling is hand-written) | pool → due jobs (start tag, close); the next alarm is the earliest pending job; done marks | low | actors `_actor_alarms` (`ORDER BY time ASC LIMIT 1` → `setAlarm`) |

Evidence: PartitelleBot, whose rules are "free of storage and Telegram", is the only prior-art bot
with real tests (35 files, Gherkin features against a fake Telegram, `test/features/telegram_world.py`).
PadelDubaiBot, Matt0550 (one 50 KB `src/main.py`) and PUBobot2 mix rules into handlers and have none.

### Reuse
| Library | Version · date | Signal | Risks |
|---|---|---|---|
| @grammyjs/parse-mode | 2.3.0 · 2026-03-13, no deps | low risk | `fmt`, `FormattedString.join`, `mentionUser(text, id)` (a `tg://user?id=` link); every send and edit must carry `entities`; Workers fit [inferred] |
| plain HTML | — | alternative | escape `<`, `>`, `&`; a mention by id works only as an inline link |
| @grammyjs/commands | 1.4.0 · 2026-07-26 | optional | the real gain is syncing the command menu (`setCommands`, scopes); core `bot.command` already rejects `/cmd@otherbot` |
| @grammyjs/chat-members | 1.2.0 · 2025-03-05 | filters only | `chatMemberFilter("out","in")` resolves `restricted`; its storage part has no Durable Object adapter |
| @grammyjs/auto-retry | 2.0.2 · 2024-07-30 | with caps | unbounded by default; caps must keep the worst case under `webhookCallback`'s 10 s; 5xx and network errors back off 3 s → 1 h unless `rethrowInternalServerErrors` / `rethrowHttpErrors` |
| @grammyjs/menu | 1.5.0 · 2026-08-27 | conditional | stateless (the pool id as `payload`), but a changed shape shows "Menu was outdated, try again!" (the one-time 🎲, parallel taps); menus must exist at startup; ties rendering to `ctx` |
| callback-data | 1.1.1 · 2023-09-18 | stale | E6 replaces it |
| Temporal (native) | flag `temporal`, default only from compatibility date 2026-12-01 | set the flag | `Temporal.Now` follows `Date.now()`; types via `lib: ["esnext"]` |
| temporal-polyfill | 1.0.8 · 2026-11-04, 19.2 kB gz | fallback | the ponyfill import "uses native if available" |
| @cloudflare/actors | 0.0.1-beta.6 · 2025-09-15 | avoid | stalled beta; a throwing job is logged and deleted, never retried |
| agents (`agents/lifecycle` Scheduler) | 0.33.0 · 2026-11-03 | possible | installs on a plain object; owns the alarm ("Do not call `ctx.storage.setAlarm()`"); 3 attempts; pre-1.0 (0.7 → 0.33 during 2026); 11 deps + 21 peers |
| hand-written jobs table | — | possible | one table, re-arm after each write, done marks |
| Drizzle | not checked | optional | official Durable Object guide: `drizzle-orm/durable-sqlite/migrator`, `migrate()` in the constructor |

### Don't build
1. A repository, ORM or unit-of-work over the object's SQLite: `sql.exec()` is synchronous, its
   cursor must be consumed "before the next await", and correctness rests on no await between read,
   decide and write (wave 2); an async repository hides exactly that. PartitelleBot keeps named SQL
   in one module, without an ORM.
2. An i18n framework: one language. Ukrainian plurals (one/few/many: гравець, гравці, гравців) are
   `Intl.PluralRules('uk')` plus a strings module.
3. Multi-chat configuration: out of scope; one allowed chat id.
4. An event bus or event sourcing: grammY middleware dispatches, and stats are a `GROUP BY` over an
   append-only table.
5. A DI container: `env` is passed explicitly, transformers fake Telegram, pure modules take `now`
   and the RNG.
6. A database-adapter interface: the platform is locked.
7. grammY sessions and conversations: sessions assume updates arrive one at a time per chat, false
   for button taps; there are no multi-step dialogs.
8. Throttling or cooldowns: the brief has none, and grammY advises against proactive throttling.
9. A natural-language time parser: chrono-node parses Ukrainian but takes offsets, not IANA zones,
   so Kyiv's DST would still be ours; a fixed grammar (E4) is smaller.
10. Menus created per pool at runtime: the menu plugin says this leaks memory.

Gotchas: SQLite can't compute Kyiv months (its `localtime` is the host's UTC; no IANA zones), so
month windows come from code (E3). The Agents scheduler takes over the alarm, and a hand-written
`setAlarm` breaks it. Button `style` and `disabled` (Bot API 10.3) are available for the card.

## Decisions for create's Decide stage
Product (Taras):
- /pool grammar: which time forms, whether a past time means tomorrow or an error, game names with
  spaces, size bounds.
- "Pool full": announced once, or again each time a drop-out refills it.
- The group's time zone: Europe/Kyiv, assumed.

Structure and stack:
- C1 Layout: feature-first (`src/pools`, `src/stats`, `src/members`, `src/chat`) vs layer-first
  (`src/bot/{features,keyboards,callback-data}`, `src/storage`).
- C2 Object naming: `ChatRoom` / `CHAT_ROOM` vs `ChatDO` vs `<name>.do.ts`.
- C3 Object declaration: `exports` (the docs) vs `migrations` (the templates still ship it).
- C4 Migrations: an ordered list module vs a private `migrate()` vs `.sql` files vs Drizzle.
- C5 Texts: a `src/texts.ts` dictionary vs Fluent (`.ftl` isn't a default Wrangler text type).
- C6 Setup: one `scripts/configure-telegram.ts` vs two scripts vs an in-Worker route vs a build
  step; run by Node, tsx or Bun.
- C7 Secrets and names: `.dev.vars` vs `.env`; `BOT_TOKEN`, `BOT_INFO`, the webhook secret's name.
- C8 Formatter and TypeScript: Prettier (C3) vs Biome vs ESLint; TS 7 vs 5.9 / 6.0.
- C9 Formatting: parse-mode entities vs HTML with a three-character escaper.
- C10 Keyboard: @grammyjs/menu vs an own codec with `bot.callbackQuery(regex)`.
- C11 Command menu: @grammyjs/commands vs one `setMyCommands` call.
- C12 Roster: chat-members filters vs hand-written ones; what makes someone a member.
- C13 Scheduling: a hand-written jobs table vs `agents/lifecycle`.
- C14 Pool-rules shape: decide → outcome (PartitelleBot) vs a reducer; pool state derived from answer
  events vs stored, with events appended for stats.
- C15 Mention chunk size: a parameter, 5 until the live test.

Tests:
- T1 Telegram fake: a recording transformer vs MSW at api.telegram.org.
- T2 Update fixtures: own builders vs `grammy-testing`.
- T3 Isolation inside a file: a unique chat id per test vs `reset()`.
- T4 Clock: an injected `now`; alarms by backdating rows and `runDurableObjectAlarm`.
- T5 Draw: an injected picker.
- T6 Layout: `test/unit` (Node) + `test/worker` projects vs co-located suffixes vs one workerd project;
  `.test.ts` vs `.spec.ts`.
- T7 Deploy gate: a required Actions check on main vs tests in the Builds command vs wrangler-action.
